text:
[Item 1: Business travel from Hangzhou to Beijing for a project seminar (intercity transportation, lodging, meal allowance, city transportation)]
Step 1: Check — Business Trip Report Form completed, signed by unit head, and affixed with the official seal of the first-level budget unit; not a trip taken by the unit head personally. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Lodging standard filled in according to bureau-director-level personnel (Professor Wang is a professor, bureau-director-level equivalent). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Compute — Beijing lodging limit for bureau-director-level personnel: RMB 650 per person per night (Appendix 1). Result: 650.
Step 4: Check — Actual hotel rate of RMB 600 per night is within the RMB 650 limit; 2 nights × RMB 600 = RMB 1,200. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — Intercity transportation was first-class train seating. Bureau-director-level personnel may be reimbursed for first-class soft seat / first-class seat on high-speed rail or EMU. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — Both intercity transportation invoice and lodging invoice are attached as required by Rule 7(4). Result: PASS.
Step 7: Check — No case of transportation or lodging being unable to be obtained, and no case of an external institution bearing intercity transportation, lodging, meal subsidy, or city transportation expenses. Result: PASS.
Step 8: Compute — Meal allowance: 3 calendar days × RMB 100/day (Beijing is in 'other regions,' not Xinjiang/Qinghai/Tibet) = RMB 300. Result: 300.
Step 9: Check — Meal allowance of RMB 300 is consistent with the Rule 7(8) calculation; intercity transportation and lodging invoices are available, so meal allowance may be claimed per Rule 7(6). Result: PASS.
Step 10: Check — City transportation of RMB 180 reimbursed against actual receipts (no self-driving or car rental); Rule 7(9) allows reimbursement against invoices within the budget limit. Result: PASS.
Step 11: Check — No self-driving or car rental involved (per Rule 7(10), local transportation allowance shall not be paid if self-driving/rental; this does not affect the present actual-receipt reimbursement). Result: PASS.
Step 12: Conclusion — All relevant travel expense requirements under Rule 7 (and general materials/invoice rules) are satisfied. The travel expense item is fully reimbursable. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Office supplies (office stationery, newspapers, and magazines) purchased after the seminar]
Step 1: Check — Items purchased are office stationery, newspapers, and magazines, which are explicitly listed in Rule 6(1) as routine office supplies charged under office expenses. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Amount does not reach the fixed asset threshold (RMB 1,000 per unit), so it is not treated as a fixed asset under Rule 16. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Items do not fall within the Asset Management Office's review scope for externally purchased inventory, so the 'Purchased Inventory Review Result Confirmation Form' is not required. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — For office supplies outside the Asset Management Office's review scope, Rule 6(2) requires either a seller-provided goods list or an online purchase transaction detail record. The seller provided a goods list together with the invoice. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — The case does not involve books and reference materials (RMB 1,000+ books requiring library registration), printing and production fees, page charges, or monograph publication subsidies, so other Rule 6 sub-clauses do not apply. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — General requirements under Rule 3 (reservation reimbursement form, signatures, original invoice) and Rule 4 (invoice negative list) apply as baseline requirements; the case describes properly organized reimbursement documents with the seller's goods list and invoice attached. Result: PASS.
Step 7: Conclusion — All applicable Rule 6 requirements are satisfied, and no conflicting rules apply. The office supplies expense is fully reimbursable. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 1: Large centrifuge maintenance expenses]
Step 1: Check — Whether the maintenance application was submitted through the Asset Management Office system as required by Rule 17. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether the 'Fudan University Fixed Asset Maintenance Application Form' was printed out. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Whether the form bears the signatures of the relevant personnel. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Whether the form is affixed with the official seal of the affiliated school or unit. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — Whether the original supporting invoice for the maintenance service is attached. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — Whether the invoice shows any of the negative-list defects under Rule 4 (missing seal, altered amount, inconsistency between words and figures, etc.). Result: PASS.
Step 7: Conclusion — All conditions of the primary rule (Rule 17) and the general material/invoice requirements (Rules 3 and 4) are satisfied; the maintenance expense is reimbursable. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Office supplies (stationery, newspapers, magazines) for the maintenance ledger]
Step 1: Check — Whether the purchased items (office stationery, newspapers, magazines) are classified as routine office supplies under Rule 6(1). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether the per-item amount is below the RMB 1,000 fixed asset threshold defined in Rule 16(1), so the items are not fixed assets. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Whether the items fall within the Asset Management Office's purchased-inventory review scope, which would require the 'Purchased Inventory Review Result Confirmation Form'. Result: FAIL (the case confirms they do NOT fall within that scope).
Step 4: Check — Whether, because the items fall outside that scope, the case provides either a seller-provided goods list or an online purchase transaction detail record under Rule 6(2). Result: PASS (seller provided a goods list with the invoice).
Step 5: Check — Whether the case involves a single book/set at RMB 1,000 or above that would trigger Humanities and Social Sciences Library registration under Rule 6(3). Result: PASS (case explicitly excludes books and materials; per-item amount is below the threshold).
Step 6: Check — Whether printing/production fees or monograph publication subsidies are involved (Rule 6(5)–(6)). Result: PASS (case explicitly excludes printing, production, and publication contracts).
Step 7: Check — Whether the invoice bears the project principal investigator's and handling staff member's signatures as required by Rule 3(2). Result: PASS.
Step 8: Check — Whether the invoice displays any negative-list defect under Rule 4. Result: PASS.
Step 9: Conclusion — All conditions of Rule 6 (office expenses branch) and the general material/invoice requirements of Rules 3 and 4 are satisfied; the office supplies are reimbursable. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 1: Final settlement payment for university history museum renovation]
Step 1: Check — Original 'Fudan University Approval Form for Engineering Project Payments and Large Cash Fund Payments' is submitted and complete. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Official seal of 'Fudan University Capital Construction Office' and 'Project Review Seal of the Fudan University Renovation Management Office' are affixed. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — For project exceeding RMB 100,000, approval signatures of the director of the Capital Construction Office and the vice president in charge are obtained. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Original 'Fudan University Construction Project Cost Review Opinion' with cost review company seal and Capital Construction Office review process seal is attached. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — Original 'Fudan University Construction Project Final Settlement Audit Filing Form' with project management department signature/seal and Audit Office receipt is attached. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — Payment amount is controlled according to the contract and project progress with no overpayment (Rule 14(2)). Result: PASS.
Step 7: Check — For payment exceeding RMB 30,000, a signed contract bearing the contract seal is provided (Rule 3(4)). Result: PASS.
Step 8: Conclusion — All Rule 14 and Rule 3 requirements for engineering final settlement are met. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Domestic official hospitality during construction communication]
Step 1: Check — Number of accompanying diners (3) does not exceed the limit of 3 when the number of guests is 10 or fewer. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — No lodging expense claimed, complying with the prohibition on charging accommodation for official activities. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Working meal standard of RMB 100 per person per day does not exceed the ordinary meal limit (Rule 18(3)). Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Banquet standard of RMB 150 per person does not exceed the upper limit for working meals when appropriately arranged (Rule 18(3)). Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — Official letter from the visiting institution is attached as required by Rule 18(1). Result: FAIL.
Step 6: Check — 'Fudan University Domestic Official Hospitality Approval Form' is attached as required by Rule 18(1). Result: FAIL.
Step 7: Conclusion — Rule 18(1) requires both the official letter and the Domestic Official Hospitality Approval Form; since one is absent, the essential material is missing. Result: Not Reimbursable.

[Item 3: Master's thesis defense labor service fees]
Step 1: Check — Number of reviewers (3) is within the required range of 2 to 3 reviewers for master's thesis. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Reviewer fee of RMB 300 per person is within the standard range of RMB 200 to 300 per person. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Number of defense committee members (5) is within the required range of 3 to 5 for master's thesis. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Committee member fee of RMB 300 per person is within the standard range of RMB 200 to 300 per person. Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — Number of defense secretaries (1) matches the required count. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — Defense secretary fee of RMB 100 matches the standard exactly. Result: PASS.
Step 7: Conclusion — All Rule 13(1) standards for master's thesis defense fees are satisfied. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 4: Academician lecture fees]
Step 1: Check — The lecturer is an academician, qualifying for the special academician standard tier. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Lecture fee of RMB 1,400 per class hour does not exceed the academician upper limit of RMB 1,500 per class hour. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Total of 4 class hours does not exceed the maximum of 4 class hours per half day under reasonable distribution. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Lecture fees are calculated based on actual class hours delivered (4 class hours at the stated rate). Result: PASS.
Step 5: Conclusion — All Rule 13(2) standards for academician lecture fees are met. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 5: Expert consulting fees (written/remote consultation)]
Step 1: Check — The consulting was carried out by communication (written/remote), falling under the written or remote consultation category. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Fee of RMB 80 per project is within the range of RMB 60 to 100 per project for persons with senior professional technical titles (and at the upper bound of RMB 40 to 80 for other personnel). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Conclusion — Rule 13(3) standard for written/remote expert consulting fees is met. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 1: Travel Expenses (Business Trip)]
Step 1: Check — Business Trip Report Form is provided with responsible person's signature and official seal. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Intercity transportation receipts are provided. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Lodging invoice for 2 nights at RMB 600/night is provided. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Compute — Trip covers 3 natural calendar days. Result: 3.
Step 5: Compute — Meal allowance standard for 'other regions' is RMB 100 per person per day (Section 8). Result: 100.
Step 6: Compute — Meal allowance claimed: 3 days × RMB 100 = RMB 300. Result: 300.
Step 7: Check — The conference organizer uniformly arranged meals and lodging for the 2-day conference per Section 5; meal allowance must NOT be paid during the conference period. Result: FAIL.
Step 8: Compute — Permissible meal allowance: only 1 non-conference day × RMB 100 = RMB 100; over-claim = RMB 300 - RMB 100 = RMB 200. Result: 200.
Step 9: Check — City transportation of RMB 180 reimbursed on actual basis (against invoices), below the 3-day lump-sum cap of RMB 240. Result: PASS.
Step 10: Conclusion — Travel expenses are partially reimbursable; the meal allowance over-claim of RMB 200 attributable to the 2 conference days must be excluded. Result: Partially Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Conference Expenses (Academic Annual Meeting)]
Step 1: Check — Conference is supported by research funds, so the research-project comprehensive quota applies (Section 1.1). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Conference duration is 2 days, within the 2-day limit for domestic business conferences (Section 7). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Quota ceiling for domestic business conferences: lodging 500 + meals 150 + other 100 = total 750 per person per day (Section 1.1). Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Conference per-person-per-day costs: lodging ~500, meals ~150, other ~110, total ~760, which exceeds the RMB 750 comprehensive quota. Result: FAIL.
Step 5: Compute — Per-person-per-day overage: RMB 760 - RMB 750 = RMB 10. Result: 10.
Step 6: Compute — Total person-days: 100 participants × 2 days = 200 person-days. Result: 200.
Step 7: Compute — Total quota overage: RMB 10 × 200 = RMB 2,000. Result: 2000.
Step 8: Check — Required supporting materials provided: conference notice and agenda, budget form, expense details, sign-in sheet, and service contract/agreement (Section 2). Result: PASS.
Step 9: Conclusion — Conference expenses exceed the comprehensive quota by approximately RMB 2,000; the portion within the quota is reimbursable, the excess is not. Result: Partially Reimbursable.

[Item 3: Office Stationery Purchase with Artificial Invoice Splitting]
Step 1: Check — Office stationery is supported by a sales list and an invoice. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — The case states 'artificial splitting of invoice amounts', which is expressly prohibited by Section 5 when used to avoid the detailed-list requirement for amounts >RMB 1,000. Result: FAIL.
Step 3: Conclusion — Artificial invoice splitting is a direct violation of Rule 6 Section 5; the purchase is not reimbursable. Result: Not Reimbursable.

[Item 4: Office Stationery and Computer Accessories Purchase]
Step 1: Check — Office stationery is supported by a sales list, satisfying Section 2 for items outside the Asset Management Office's review scope. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Computer accessories fall within the Asset Management Office's purchased-inventory review scope per Section 2 and therefore require the 'Fudan University Purchased Inventory Review Result Confirmation Form'. Result: FAIL.
Step 3: Check — The required Asset Management Office confirmation form is NOT provided for the computer accessories portion. Result: FAIL.
Step 4: Check — No breakdown between the office stationery portion and the computer accessories portion is provided, so a partial reimbursement amount cannot be determined. Result: FAIL.
Step 5: Conclusion — An essential material (the Asset Management Office confirmation form) is missing for the computer accessories portion, and no breakdown is available to allow partial reimbursement; the purchase as presented is not reimbursable. Result: Not Reimbursable.

[Item 1: Training Expenses (20-day teaching methodology training)]
Step 1: Check — Whether the 'Fudan University Detailed List of Training Expense Expenditures' approved by the school/department is provided. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether the trainee list and contact information is provided per Rule 10(3). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Whether the detailed expense statement and invoices from the training service provider are provided. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Whether the training duration (20 days) is within the ≤30-day full comprehensive quota standard per Rule 10(2). Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — Whether the training is properly reported at bureau-director-level standard (650 RMB per person per day). Result: PASS.
Step 6: Compute — Comprehensive quota items: 18,720 (total including 2,500 lecturer fees) - 2,500 = 16,220 RMB over 20 days = 811 RMB per day total. Result: 811 RMB per day total.
Step 7: Check — Whether the per-trainee-per-day comprehensive quota does not exceed the 650 RMB bureau-director-level cap. Result: FAIL (the case provides a complete trainee list but does not state the trainee count, so per-person verification cannot be completed independently).
Step 8: Compute — Instructor fees calculated separately per Rule 10(4): 2,500 (lecture fees) + 600 (lodging) + 200 (meals) + 900 (transportation) = 4,200 RMB. Result: 4,200 RMB instructor fees (separate from quota).
Step 9: Conclusion — Required materials are complete and instructor fees are properly separated from the comprehensive quota, but the per-trainee cap cannot be verified without the number of trainees. Result: Pending.

[Item 2: Travel Expenses (intercity transportation and lodging)]
Step 1: Check — Whether intercity transportation receipts are provided. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether the lodging invoice is provided. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Whether the responsible person's signature and official seal are complete. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Whether the 'Fudan University Business Trip Report Form' is attached per Rule 7(1). Result: FAIL (case explicitly states the form was not attached).
Step 5: Check — Whether the business trip approval and itinerary materials are attached per Rule 3(3). Result: FAIL (case explicitly states these were not attached).
Step 6: Conclusion — The Business Trip Report Form and business trip approval/itinerary materials required by Rule 7(1) and Rule 3(3) are missing; this is an essential material. Result: Not Reimbursable.

[Item 3: Special Lecture Fees (8 class hours at 500 RMB per class hour)]
Step 1: Check — Whether the lecture hours (8) comply with the maximum of 4 class hours per half day per Rule 13(2). Result: PASS (8 hours = 2 half days).
Step 2: Check — Whether the lecture fee rate of 500 RMB per class hour falls within the standard for associate senior or higher professional title. Result: PASS for associate senior / full senior / academician (caps at 500 / 1,000 / 1,500).
Step 3: Check — Whether the lecturer's professional technical title is documented. Result: FAIL (case only states the lecturer is reported under the administrative category 'division-level and lower personnel', not a professional title).
Step 4: Check — Whether external personnel information (ID, bank account) is registered per Rule 12(3) if the lecturer is external. Result: FAIL (no information provided in case).
Step 5: Compute — Total lecture fees: 500 × 8 = 4,000 RMB. Result: 4,000 RMB.
Step 6: Conclusion — Cannot verify compliance with Rule 13(2) because the lecturer's professional technical title is not stated; an administrative rank cannot substitute for a professional title under Rule 13(2); if the lecturer is below associate senior, 500 RMB/class hour may exceed the 'by reference' standard for other personnel. Result: Pending.

[Item 4: On-site Consulting Fees (2 days at 800 RMB per day)]
Step 1: Check — Whether the consulting duration (2 days) is reasonable for on-site consultation. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether 800 RMB per day falls within the senior professional range of 500–800 RMB per day per Rule 13(3) (first and second days). Result: PASS for senior professional technical title (at the upper cap).
Step 3: Check — Whether 800 RMB per day falls within the 'other personnel' range of 300–500 RMB per day per Rule 13(3). Result: FAIL (800 RMB per day exceeds the 500 RMB cap for other personnel).
Step 4: Check — Whether the consultant's professional technical title is documented. Result: FAIL (case does not specify the consultant's professional title).
Step 5: Check — Whether external personnel information (ID, bank account) is registered per Rule 12(3) if the consultant is external. Result: FAIL (no information provided in case).
Step 6: Compute — Total consulting fees: 800 × 2 = 1,600 RMB. Result: 1,600 RMB.
Step 7: Conclusion — Cannot verify compliance with Rule 13(3) without the consultant's professional technical title; if the consultant lacks senior professional title, 800 RMB/day exceeds the 300–500 RMB/day cap for other personnel. Result: Pending.

[Item 5: Small Purchases - Office Stationery and Drinking Water for course preparation]
Step 1: Check — Whether office stationery and drinking water fall within the office expense category per Rule 6(1). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether the items fall below the fixed asset threshold (per unit under 1,000 RMB) so no asset registration is required. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Whether the items fall within the Asset Management Office's inventory review scope (no, they are routine low-value office supplies). Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Whether a sales list from the seller is attached per Rule 6(2). Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — Whether an original invoice is provided with required signatures per Rule 3. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Conclusion — All required materials are provided and the items fall within the office expense category under Rule 6. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 1: Family Visit Travel Expenses (Unmarried employee visiting parents)]
Step 1: Check — Whether the claimant qualifies as an unmarried faculty member visiting parents (Article 11(1)). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether the expense is restricted to intercity transportation only, with no local transportation (Article 11(3)). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Whether the 'Fudan University Faculty and Staff Family Visit Application and Approval Form' was submitted with department approval and Human Resources Office seal (Article 11(4)). Result: FAIL.
Step 4: Conclusion — The family visit application form is an essential material under Article 11(4); without it, the case cannot be processed. Result: Not Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Travel Expenses (trip to conference - first-class train, 2 nights lodging, meal subsidy, local transportation)]
Step 1: Check — Whether the Business Trip Report Form was completed and countersigned (the unit head traveled personally, so countersigned by another leader) (Article 7(1)). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether the transportation class complies with bureau-director/professor rank: first-class seat on high-speed rail/EMU is permitted (Article 7(2)). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Whether lodging at RMB 600/night complies with the bureau-director level accommodation limit for the destination city (Article 7(3) and Appendix 1). Result: PASS.
Step 4: Compute — Meal allowance claimed = 3 days × RMB 100/day = RMB 300. Result: .
Step 5: Check — Whether the conference uniformly arranged meals and lodging (per conference description), in which case no meal allowance or transportation subsidy shall be paid during the 1-day conference period (Article 7(5)). Result: FAIL.
Step 6: Compute — Allowable meal allowance = 2 non-conference days × RMB 100 = RMB 200 (1 conference day excluded); claimed excess = RMB 100. Result: .
Step 7: Compute — Lump-sum local transportation claimed = 3 days × RMB 80 = RMB 240. Result: .
Step 8: Compute — Allowable lump-sum local transportation = 2 non-conference days × RMB 80 = RMB 160 (1 conference day excluded); claimed excess = RMB 80. Result: .
Step 9: Conclusion — Transportation and lodging are reimbursable; meal subsidy and local transportation are partially reimbursable due to the 1-day conference exclusion. Result: Partially Reimbursable. Result: Partially Reimbursable.

[Item 3: Conference Expenses (domestic management conference, non-research funds, ~100 participants, 1 day)]
Step 1: Check — Whether the conference materials are complete as listed in Article 9(2) (notice, budget form, sign-in sheet, invoices, etc.). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether the conference category and funding source are properly identified (domestic management conference, non-research funds), so the central/state organs Category III and IV quota (340/130/80, total 550) applies. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Compute — Quota per person per day: accommodation 340, meals 130, other 80, total 550. Result: .
Step 4: Compute — Actual per person per day: accommodation 340, meals 130, other 90, total 560. Result: .
Step 5: Compute — Overage per person per day = 560 − 550 = RMB 10. Result: .
Step 6: Compute — Total person-days ≈ 100 participants × 1 day = 100 person-days; total overage = 100 × RMB 10 = RMB 1,000 (exceeds comprehensive quota; cannot be reallocated since lodging and meals are already at their item limits). Result: .
Step 7: Conclusion — Conference expenses within the comprehensive quota are reimbursable; the RMB 10 per person per day overage (RMB 1,000 total) exceeds the comprehensive quota and is not reimbursable. Result: Partially Reimbursable. Result: Partially Reimbursable.

[Item 4: Doctoral Dissertation Defense Fees]
Step 1: Check — Whether the case identifies this as a doctoral thesis defense under Article 13(1). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether the case provides the number of reviewers (5–8), defense committee members (5–7), the secretary, and specific amounts per person required to verify compliance with Article 13(1). Result: FAIL.
Step 3: Conclusion — Without specific numbers (number of reviewers, committee members, secretary, and individual amounts) in the case description, compliance with Article 13(1) cannot be verified; item is pending submission/verification of these details. Result: Pending. Result: Pending.

[Item 5: Lecture Fees (bureau-level personnel, 4 class hours × RMB 900)]
Step 1: Check — Whether the lecturer's rank qualifies under Article 13(2). Bureau-level personnel correspond to full senior technical titles (professor/research fellow level). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Whether the lecture fee rate complies with the Article 13(2) cap of RMB 1,000 per class hour for full senior technical titles (RMB 900 < RMB 1,000). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Whether the number of class hours complies with the Article 13(2) limit of 4 class hours per half day (4 class hours = maximum permitted for one half day). Result: PASS.
Step 4: Compute — Total lecture fee = 4 × RMB 900 = RMB 3,600. Result: .
Step 5: Conclusion — Lecture fee rate, class hours, and total comply with Article 13(2). Result: Fully Reimbursable. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 1: Overseas travel expenses for the Germany international education exhibition]
Step 1: Check — Traveler's rank (bureau-director-level and above). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Applicable airfare class standard for bureau-director-level personnel under research project funds (per Rule 8(3) routing to Rule 7(2)). Result: Economy class airfare.
Step 3: Check — Actual air ticket class purchased (first-class). Result: FAIL — first-class exceeds the economy class standard.
Step 4: Check — Foreign affairs approval document attached (per Rule 8(1)). Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — Overseas expense reimbursement form attached, listing registration fee, living allowance, incidental expenses, transportation expenses (per Rule 8(1)). Result: PASS.
Step 6: Compute — Non-reimbursable excess = first-class airfare minus economy class airfare equivalent. Result: Excess portion (difference between first-class and economy class).
Step 7: Conclusion — The first-class airfare exceeds the bureau-director-level economy class standard for research funds, while other items (registration fee, living allowance, incidental expenses) appear within standard. Result: Partially Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Domestic management conference expenses]
Step 1: Check — Conference type (domestic management conference) and fund source (non-research project funds), so central/state organs standards apply (per Rule 9(1)). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Applicable conference category. The actual per-person lodging (340) and meals (130) match the Category III/IV standards, so Category III/IV is presumed. Result: Category III/IV.
Step 3: Check — Comprehensive quota for Category III/IV (per Rule 9(1) and Appendix 2). Result: Accommodation 340, Meals 130, Other 80, Total 550.
Step 4: Check — Actual per-person-per-day expenses. Result: Accommodation 340, Meals 130, Other 90, Total 560.
Step 5: Compute — Excess over the comprehensive quota (560 − 550). Result: 10 RMB per person per day.
Step 6: Compute — Total non-reimbursable amount (≈ 10 RMB × 100 participants × 1 day). Result: ≈ 1000 RMB.
Step 7: Check — Conference duration (1 day) does not exceed the 1-day limit for domestic management conferences (per Rule 9(7)). Result: PASS.
Step 8: Check — Required materials: conference notice, agenda, budget form, detailed expense list, sign-in sheet of actual participants, and service contract/agreement (per Rule 9(2)). Result: PASS.
Step 9: Conclusion — Other-expense item exceeds the 80 standard and pushes total over the 550 comprehensive quota; other materials and duration are compliant. Result: Partially Reimbursable.

[Item 3: Application software purchase (intangible asset)]
Step 1: Check — Application software value: assumed to be ≥ RMB 2,000 (since the intangible asset reimbursement form was attached). Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Application software is not an indispensable component of related hardware (per Rule 16(2)). Result: PASS (assumed).
Step 3: Check — Second copy of the 'Fudan University Asset Reimbursement Form (Intangible Assets)' issued by the Asset Management Office is attached (per Rule 16(2)). Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Original supporting invoice bearing signatures of the project principal investigator and the handling staff member (per Rule 3(2)). Result: PASS (assumed).
Step 5: Conclusion — Materials required by Rule 16(2) and Rule 3 are in place; nothing in the case indicates a violation. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 4: Small purchase of office stationery and office furniture]
Step 1: Check — Office furniture unit price is below the RMB 1,000 fixed asset threshold (per Rule 16(1)). Result: PASS (assumed from 'small purchase').
Step 2: Check — Items do not fall within the Asset Management Office's purchased-inventory review scope (per Rule 6(2)), so a sales list is acceptable. Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — Sales list provided by the seller is attached together with the invoice (per Rule 6(2)). Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — Original supporting invoice bearing signatures of the project principal investigator and the handling staff member (per Rule 3(2)). Result: PASS (assumed).
Step 5: Conclusion — Items qualify as office expenses, materials under Rule 6(2) and Rule 3 are in place, no obvious violation. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 1: Engineering final settlement payment for the restroom renovation project]
Step 1: Check — The original 'Fudan University Approval Form for Engineering Project Payments and Large Cash Fund Payments' approved by the Capital Construction Office is provided. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — The approval form bears the official seal of 'Fudan University Capital Construction Office' as required by Rule 14(1). Result: PASS.
Step 3: Check — The approval form bears the 'Project Review Seal of the Fudan University Renovation Management Office'. Result: PASS.
Step 4: Check — The engineering amount exceeds RMB 100,000, triggering the additional approval-signature requirement under Rule 14(1). Result: PASS.
Step 5: Check — The approval form bears the signature of the director of the Capital Construction Office. Result: PASS.
Step 6: Check — The approval form bears the signature of the vice president in charge. Result: PASS.
Step 7: Check — The original 'Fudan University Construction Project Cost Review Opinion' is attached as required by Rule 14(4). Result: PASS.
Step 8: Check — The original 'Fudan University Construction Project Final Settlement Audit Filing Form' is attached as required by Rule 14(4). Result: PASS.
Step 9: Check — The payment amount is controlled according to the contract and project progress, with no overpayment, as required by Rule 14(2). Result: PASS.
Step 10: Conclusion — All approval, seal, signature, supporting-document, and payment-amount requirements of Rule 14 are satisfied. Result: Fully Reimbursable.

[Item 2: Warranty retention refund for the renovation engineering/equipment]
Step 1: Check — The engineering/equipment invoice had been provided and the warranty retention portion had been included when the invoice was originally issued. Result: PASS.
Step 2: Check — Finance had issued a dedicated warranty retention receipt according to the warranty retention ratio. Result: PASS.
